property_summary: If C.transfer returns (i.e., does not revert) then it always returns true and leaves c.from unchanged and c.caddress unchanged.

If transfer does not revert then it returns (i.e., call succeeds) and the c.from getter remains equal to the known hardcoded sender address encoded in the contract (so c.from() equals its value before the call).
For any non-empty matching-length inputs, if C.transfer does not revert then it returns true (call succeeds) and the public caddress getter remains unchanged.
For any non-empty equal-length inputs where transfer is called, if the call does not revert then c.caddress() remains equal to its value observed before the call.

property_summary: If transfer returns (i.e., does not revert) then it returns true and does not change C.from or C.caddress public getters.
If transfer returns (doesn't revert) then it returns true.
If transfer does not revert then it returns true and does not modify the public from or caddress getters.
For any non-empty matched arrays, if transfer does not revert then it returns true.
For any non-empty equal-length arrays where every v[i] is either zero or fits when multiplied/divided by 1e18, the transfer call either reverts or returns true (i.e., it cannot return false).
If transfer(...) returns (i.e., does not revert) then it must return true and the c.from and c.caddress public getters remain unchanged.
If transfer(...) does not revert when called by this contract, it must return true.
